title: the exact equality |dq| = astq answers YES (>=) in float32 and in float64
derivation: Target offset x = radius / 3 puts it exactly on the astq cone: d2 = 10^2 + 40^2 = 1700, dq = 40 / sqrt(1700) and astq = sqrt(1 - 30^2 / (9 x 1700)) = sqrt(1600 / 1700), the same number. Oolite computes dq, d2, radius, aim and astq as GLfloat (9855-9907): the self-test evaluates this pose with every step rounded to float32 (dq = astq = 0.9701424837112427) and in float64 (dq = astq = 0.9701425001453319): both widths compare equal, so the answer is the same in both. Other exact-equality poses (for example (10, 0, 23) with radius 30) round differently in the two widths and a float64 port answers NO there while Oolite's float32 answers YES; the self-test records that difference but no fixture demands it.
